Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review community source code before installing or running it. ## Get started You need Python 3.11+, [uv](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/install/uv.html), and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows. Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project. This example uses GitHub Copilot. ```bash uv tool install specify-cli specify init my-project --integration copilot cd my-project ``` After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding agent in the project directory, then choose a process below. For other setups: - [Installation](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/installation.html) for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting. - [Existing projects](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/existing-projects.html) to start with code you already have. - [Other agents](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/index.html) for integration keys and [invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). - [Upgrade](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/upgrade.html) to update an existing installation. ## Spec-Driven Development Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks, and working code. The minimal flow is shown below. Create a constitution once per project and repeat the remaining steps for each feature. Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability. /speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album. /speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite. /speckit-tasks /speckit-implement /speckit-converge ``` Repeat implement and converge until convergence reports `Converged`. For clarification, checklists, and consistency analysis, see the SDD walkthrough. [SDD walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/quickstart.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-sdd.html) ## Bug fixing Assess the cause, fix the bug, and verify the original symptom is resolved. No SDD feature workflow is required first. Install the bug-fixing extension in your terminal, from the project directory: ```bash specify extension add bug ``` Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash /speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash ``` Review the reports in `.specify/bugs/login-crash/`. The final verdict is `verified`, `partial`, or `failed`; only `verified` confirms a successful fix. [Bug-fixing walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/bugfix.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-bugfix.html) ## Idea assessment Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing. No source code or SDD feature workflow is required. Install the assessment extension in your terminal, from the project directory: ```bash specify extension add assess ``` Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing. This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its [equivalent invocation syntax](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/integrations/cli.html#command-invocation). ```text /speckit-assess-intake "Let users work offline and sync when they reconnect." slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-research slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-define slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-shape slug=offline-mode /speckit-assess-decide slug=offline-mode ``` Review the artifacts in `.specify/assessments/offline-mode/` and the final decision: `go`, `needs-clarification`, or `kill`. Resolve unknowns by editing the existing Markdown artifacts, directly or with your agent, rather than rerunning whole stages. If you choose to build a software idea with a `go` decision, establish a project constitution if needed, then pass the handoff summary from `decision.md` to `/speckit-specify`. Stopping with a documented reason is also a useful outcome. [Assessment walkthrough](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/guides/assessment.html) · [Command reference](https://github.github.io/spec-kit/reference/agentic-assessment.html) ## Customize or bring your own process Customize Spec-Driven Development, bug fixing, or idea assessment to fit your team's standards. Or bring your own process without adopting any of them. Combine the [capabilities above](#capabilities) to match your goal: - Adapt an existing process with a preset, such as requiring regulatory traceability in plans. Use a project-local override for a one-off template change. - Bring your own process by adding its commands through an extension and exposing them to your coding agent through an integration. - Automate commands and checks in a workflow. Use overlays to adapt an installed workflow without forking it, or add custom workflow steps when the built-in types are not enough. - Share a reusable setup by packaging its extensions, presets, workflows, and workflow steps in a bundle. Start with the smallest change that meets your needs; you do not have to replace the whole process. 🌱 Spec Kit

Build with a spec, fix a bug, or assess an idea — with your coding agent.

English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Spec Kit is an open source toolkit that gives AI coding agents structured processes, reusable templates, and documented outcomes. Start with a ready-made process, customize it, or bring your own.

Choose your process

What you need Process Outcome
Build a feature or application Spec-Driven Development A specification carried through planning, implementation, and convergence
Diagnose and repair broken behavior Bug fixing An assessed cause, scoped fix, and recorded verification
Decide whether an idea deserves investment Idea assessment An evidence-backed go, clarify, or stop decision
Adopt or create a different process Your own process A process adapted or assembled from reusable primitives

These are independent entry points, not mandatory phases. SDD ships in core; bug fixing and assessment are bundled extensions you install when needed, and the primitives below let you adopt or create other processes.

Capabilities

Spec Kit combines ready-to-use processes with composable mechanisms:

Capability Spec Kit mechanism
Connect to or switch between coding agents Integration
Add a command, quality gate, or complete process Extension
Connect a process to an external tool or service Extension
React to coding-agent lifecycle events Extension runtime event
Run extension commands before or after Spec Kit commands Extension hook
Adapt templates, commands, terminology, or methodology Preset
Enforce organizational or regulatory standards Preset
Override a template for one project Project-local override
Automate prompts, commands, gates, and shell tasks Workflow
Modify an installed workflow without forking it Workflow overlay
Add reusable executable behavior to workflows Workflow step
Install a curated setup for a role or team Bundle
Discover community components Catalog
Host a private catalog of approved components Catalog
Access private catalogs and component downloads Authentication
Work offline or behind a firewall Local sources and self-hosted catalogs
Inspect which layer supplies a command, template, or script Artifact inventory

Search the active catalogs with commands such as specify extension search, specify preset search, specify workflow search, and specify bundle search. Spec Kit includes community catalogs, and organizations can add their own curated sources. Catalog listings are not audits or endorsements, so review community source code before installing or running it.

Get started

You need Python 3.11+, uv, and a supported AI coding agent on Linux, macOS, or Windows.

Run these commands in your terminal to install Spec Kit and create a project. This example uses GitHub Copilot.

uv tool install specify-cli
specify init my-project --integration copilot
cd my-project

After installing the Specify CLI and creating your project, launch your coding agent in the project directory, then choose a process below.

For other setups:

  • Installation for pinned releases, other installers, CI, and troubleshooting.
  • Existing projects to start with code you already have.
  • Other agents for integration keys and invocation syntax.
  • Upgrade to update an existing installation.

Spec-Driven Development

Define what to build and why, then turn the specification into a plan, tasks, and working code.

The minimal flow is shown below. Create a constitution once per project and repeat the remaining steps for each feature. Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its equivalent invocation syntax.

/speckit-constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing, and maintainability.
/speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album.
/speckit-plan Use Vite with vanilla JavaScript. Keep images local and store metadata in SQLite.
/speckit-tasks
/speckit-implement
/speckit-converge

Repeat implement and converge until convergence reports Converged. For clarification, checklists, and consistency analysis, see the SDD walkthrough.

SDD walkthrough · Command reference

Bug fixing

Assess the cause, fix the bug, and verify the original symptom is resolved. No SDD feature workflow is required first.

Install the bug-fixing extension in your terminal, from the project directory:

specify extension add bug

Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its equivalent invocation syntax.

/speckit-bug-assess "Submitting an empty password crashes the login form." slug=login-crash
/speckit-bug-fix slug=login-crash
/speckit-bug-test slug=login-crash

Review the reports in .specify/bugs/login-crash/. The final verdict is verified, partial, or failed; only verified confirms a successful fix.

Bug-fixing walkthrough · Command reference

Idea assessment

Gather evidence to decide whether an idea is worth pursuing. No source code or SDD feature workflow is required.

Install the assessment extension in your terminal, from the project directory:

specify extension add assess

Run these skills in your agent's chat, not your terminal, one at a time, reviewing each result before continuing.

This example uses GitHub Copilot's default skills syntax. For another agent, use its equivalent invocation syntax.

/speckit-assess-intake "Let users work offline and sync when they reconnect." slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-research slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-define slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-shape slug=offline-mode
/speckit-assess-decide slug=offline-mode

Review the artifacts in .specify/assessments/offline-mode/ and the final decision: go, needs-clarification, or kill. Resolve unknowns by editing the existing Markdown artifacts, directly or with your agent, rather than rerunning whole stages. If you choose to build a software idea with a go decision, establish a project constitution if needed, then pass the handoff summary from decision.md to /speckit-specify. Stopping with a documented reason is also a useful outcome.

Assessment walkthrough · Command reference

Customize or bring your own process

Customize Spec-Driven Development, bug fixing, or idea assessment to fit your team's standards. Or bring your own process without adopting any of them. Combine the capabilities above to match your goal:

  • Adapt an existing process with a preset, such as requiring regulatory traceability in plans. Use a project-local override for a one-off template change.
  • Bring your own process by adding its commands through an extension and exposing them to your coding agent through an integration.
  • Automate commands and checks in a workflow. Use overlays to adapt an installed workflow without forking it, or add custom workflow steps when the built-in types are not enough.
  • Share a reusable setup by packaging its extensions, presets, workflows, and workflow steps in a bundle.

Start with the smallest change that meets your needs; you do not have to replace the whole process.

Customization guide · Community components and walkthroughs

Documentation

  • CLI reference and process commands
  • SDD philosophy, full methodology, and evolving existing specs
  • Project history
  • How Spec Kit uses Spec Kit

In the news

  • Open Source Friday: Spec Kit Part 2 (October 16, 2026) — Manfred Riem and Nicole Haugen discuss Spec Kit 1.0 and the expanded toolkit.
  • Open Source Friday with Spec Kit (May 8, 2026) — An introduction and SDD demonstration with Manfred Riem.

Star history

Thanks to everyone who helps Spec Kit shine.

Support and contributing

Report a bug or request a feature · Contributing guide · Code of conduct

Spec Kit is MIT licensed.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A toolkit connecting high-level specification documents directly to executing AI agents for test-driven development.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Spec-Kit is a developer toolkit designed to bridge the gap between abstract requirements and executable code by tightly integrating specification documents with AI coding agents. It enforces a behavior-driven development workflow where product managers or engineers write detailed specifications in Markdown, and AI agents consume these documents to autonomously generate and execute corresponding test suites. The framework ensures that AI-generated code strictly adheres to the stated business logic rather than hallucinating features. It provides tools for parsing specifications, validating test coverage, and generating actionable prompts for large language models. By treating specifications as the authoritative source of truth, it creates a closed-loop system for AI-assisted software engineering.
keyFeatures: Specification parsing: Automatically extracts actionable requirements and constraints from human-readable Markdown documents.
Test generation: Guides AI agents to generate comprehensive test suites based strictly on parsed specifications.
Agent orchestration: Coordinates the interaction between the specification document, the testing framework, and the executing AI model.
Coverage validation: Analyzes the resulting codebase to ensure all specified behaviors are adequately tested and implemented.
Prompt engineering tools: Provides pre-configured, highly constrained prompts designed to keep LLMs focused on the specification.

useCases.title: Test-driven agent development
useCases.description: Use the toolkit to force AI agents to write failing tests based on specifications before generating the actual implementation code.

useCases.title: Requirements validation
useCases.description: Product managers write detailed feature specifications, which the system uses to verify that the final AI-generated code meets all business rules.

useCases.title: Automated regression testing
useCases.description: QA engineers automatically generate extensive regression test suites from updated specification documents whenever requirements change.

useCases.title: Standardizing AI output
useCases.description: Organizations enforce a strict workflow where all AI-generated code must trace back directly to a formal, tracked specification.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers, QA professionals, and technical product managers implementing behavior-driven development with AI assistants. Users need a solid understanding of testing frameworks and prompt engineering concepts.
